renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: coverage_track_amplicon
  title: Amplicon depth along the genome
  description: |-
    Each point on a line is an amplicon placed at its genome position, with its mean read depth on the vertical axis, one line per sample. It answers which amplicons are poorly covered and whether the same ones fail across samples.
    How to read: lines should stay well above zero along the genome. A dip that appears in every sample is a failing primer pair, and a dip in one sample is a sample-specific drop-out. Open the amplicon matrix to compare samples side by side.
    Lines and annotations: no line is drawn. A consensus needs enough depth at each base, and nf-core/viralrecon and iVar both call a consensus base from a depth of 10 reads by default, so dips towards that depth are where bases turn into Ns.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/viralrecon/master/docs/output.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andersen-lab/ivar/master/docs/MANUAL.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/viralrecon/master/conf/modules_illumina.config
  kind: coverage_track
  config:
    color_by: sample
  roles:
    chromosome: chrom
    position: start
    end: end
    value: coverage
    sample: sample

- component: card
  title: Amplicon depth
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median read depth of an amplicon over all samples, and the box shows the quartiles and outliers. It answers how deeply the amplicons are covered overall.
    How to read: a median far above 10 reads with a tight box means even, deep coverage. A long lower tail, or amplicons near zero, are the drop-outs that leave gaps in the consensus.
    Lines and annotations: no mark is drawn. nf-core/viralrecon and iVar call consensus bases from a depth of 10 reads by default.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/viralrecon/master/docs/output.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andersen-lab/ivar/master/docs/MANUAL.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/viralrecon/master/conf/modules_illumina.config
  column: coverage
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread
  headline: true

- component: table
  title: Amplicon coverage
  description: |-
    One row is one amplicon in one sample, with its genome coordinates and mean depth. It answers which amplicons are poorly covered.
    How to read: Sort by coverage, lowest first, to find the dropouts, and by start to read them in genome order. Look for amplicons that fail in several samples, which suggests a primer problem rather than a sample one. It complements the amplicon heatmap of the same module, which shows the same values as a grid.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: complex_heatmap
  title: Amplicon coverage matrix
  description: |-
    Each cell is an amplicon in one sample, coloured by its log10 read depth, with amplicons in genome order and samples clustered by similarity. It answers which amplicons fail and which samples fail together.
    How to read: a pale column is an amplicon with low depth in many samples, which points at a failing primer pair. A pale row is a poorly sequenced sample, and samples that cluster together share the same drop-out pattern, often from the same batch or primer scheme.
    Lines and annotations: no mark is drawn. Values are log10 of the mean amplicon depth, so 1 is 10 reads and 3 is 1000 reads.
  kind: complex_heatmap
  config:
    cluster_cols: false
    cluster_rows: true
  roles:
    index: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: cumulative_curve
  title: Cumulative coverage curve
  description: |-
    Each line is a mapping: the share of the reference covered at least at each depth, from mosdepth's global distribution. It answers how much of the genome is deep enough to call variants and a consensus.
    How to read: a curve that stays near 100 percent and falls late means even deep coverage. A curve that drops early, or a lower plateau, means part of the genome is thinly covered or not covered at all. Read the value where a curve crosses the marked line to see the breadth at that depth.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical marker is 10X, the default minimum depth at which nf-core/viralrecon calls variants and consensus bases. iVar's own default is 10 reads for a consensus base but 0 for a variant call. mosdepth itself sets no cut-off.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/viralrecon/master/docs/output.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andersen-lab/ivar/master/docs/MANUAL.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/viralrecon/master/conf/modules_illumina.config and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brentp/mosdepth/master/README.md
  kind: profile
  config:
    reference_x: 10
    reference_label: 10X, minimum depth for variant and consensus calls
    x_title: Depth (X)
    y_title: Bases covered at least this deep (%)
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: genome_id
    x: depth
    y: bases_pct

- component: card
  title: Bases covered across depths
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median, over every depth step of every mapping, of the percentage of bases covered at least that deep, and the box shows the spread. It answers how quickly coverage falls off with depth overall.
    How to read: read it next to the curve, since it pools every depth step. A high median with a tight box means most of the genome stays covered as the depth rises.
  column: bases_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Cumulative coverage
  description: |-
    One row is one mapping at one depth, with the percentage of bases covered at least that deep. It answers how much of the genome reaches a given depth.
    How to read: Filter on a depth of interest and sort by the percentage to rank the mappings. Look for a mapping whose percentage falls early as the depth rises. It complements the cumulative curve tile of the same output, which draws these rows as lines.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: coverage_track_genome
  title: Depth along the genome
  description: |-
    Each point on the line is a window of the genome at its position, with its mean read depth on the vertical axis. It answers where along the genome coverage dips.
    How to read: lines should stay well above zero across the genome. A dip shared in every run is a region that is hard to sequence or to map, or a failing amplicon. Zoom into a dip and compare it with the amplicon tile, which splits depth by sample.
    Lines and annotations: no line is drawn. nf-core/viralrecon and iVar call consensus bases from a depth of 10 reads by default.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/viralrecon/master/docs/output.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andersen-lab/ivar/master/docs/MANUAL.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/viralrecon/master/conf/modules_illumina.config
  kind: coverage_track
  roles:
    chromosome: chromosome
    position: position
    value: value

- component: card
  title: Window depth
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median mean depth of a genome window over all samples, and the box shows the quartiles and outliers. It answers how deeply the genome is covered overall.
    How to read: a median far above 10 reads with a tight box means even, deep coverage. A long lower tail holds the windows that leave gaps in a consensus.
    Lines and annotations: no mark is drawn. nf-core/viralrecon and iVar call consensus bases from a depth of 10 reads by default.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/viralrecon/master/docs/output.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andersen-lab/ivar/master/docs/MANUAL.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/viralrecon/master/conf/modules_illumina.config
  column: value
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread
  headline: true

- component: advanced_viz
  id: depth_track
  title: Binned depth along the reference
  description: |-
    Each point on a line is a bin of the reference at its position, with its length-weighted mean read depth on the vertical axis, one line per mapping. It answers where the depth drops, as dropouts or amplicon gaps, along the genome.
    How to read: lines should stay well above zero along the genome. A dip to zero is a gap that will become Ns in the consensus, and repeated dips at regular spacing are failing amplicons. Compare mappings to see whether a gap is shared.
    Lines and annotations: no line is drawn. nf-core/viralrecon and iVar call consensus bases from a depth of 10 reads by default, so bins below it are likely to be masked.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/viralrecon/master/docs/output.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andersen-lab/ivar/master/docs/MANUAL.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/viralrecon/master/conf/modules_illumina.config
  kind: coverage_track
  config:
    color_by: sample
  roles:
    chromosome: chrom
    position: position
    value: mean_depth
    end: end
    sample: genome_id

- component: card
  title: Lowest depth in any bin
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest depth found in any bin and the bars rank the mappings by their lowest bin. It answers whether any part of the genome is left uncovered.
    How to read: a value of zero means a gap in at least one mapping, which becomes Ns in a consensus. The median and maximum beside it show the typical and best cases.
    Lines and annotations: no mark is drawn. nf-core/viralrecon and iVar call consensus bases from a depth of 10 reads by default.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/viralrecon/master/docs/output.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andersen-lab/ivar/master/docs/MANUAL.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/viralrecon/master/conf/modules_illumina.config
  column: min_depth
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: genome_id
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: lowest bin depth, by mapping

- component: table
  title: Binned depth
  description: |-
    One row is one bin of one mapping, with its coordinates, mean depth and lowest depth. It answers where along the genome the depth drops.
    How to read: Sort by mean depth, lowest first, to find the weak bins, and by the lowest depth to find bins with a gap inside. Look for bins that are weak in several mappings. It complements the coverage track tile of the same output, which draws these bins along the genome.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: coverage_track_regions
  title: Target depth along the genome
  description: |-
    Each point on a line is a 1 Mb window of the genome at its position, with the target-length-weighted mean depth of the targets in it, one line per sample. It answers whether the targeted regions are covered evenly along the genome.
    How to read: lines of different samples should rise and fall together, scaled by sequencing depth. A window that drops in every sample is a difficult region or a target missing from the panel, and a window that drops in one sample is a local failure.
    Lines and annotations: no line is drawn, and mosdepth publishes no depth cut-off. Judge depth against the assay's own requirement.
  kind: coverage_track
  config:
    color_by: sample
  roles:
    chromosome: chromosome
    position: position
    value: value
    end: end
    sample: sample_stage

- component: advanced_viz
  id: genomespy_regions
  title: Target depth on the genome axis
  description: |-
    Each bar is a 1 Mb window of the genome with its target-length-weighted mean depth, on one axis that concatenates every chromosome, coloured by sample. It answers where along the whole genome the targets are covered, and lets you brush a region to filter the rest of the tab.
    How to read: bars should be of similar height across windows of a sample. A stretch of short bars is a poorly covered region, and tall bars are regions with high target density or copy gain. Brush a stretch to focus the other tiles on it.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median window depth of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of mosdepth. mosdepth publishes no depth cut-off.
  kind: genome_view
  config:
    score_title: Mean target depth (X)
    score_threshold_stat: median
  roles:
    chr: chromosome
    pos: position
    score: value
    end: end
    feature: sample_stage
    category: sample

- component: card
  title: Window depth
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median mean target depth of a 1 Mb window, and the box shows the quartiles and outliers. It answers how deeply the targets are covered overall.
    How to read: a tight box means even coverage along the genome. A long lower tail holds windows that are under-covered and may hide variants.
  column: value
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Window depth
  description: |-
    One row is one 1 Mb window of one sample, with its mean target depth and number of targets. It answers which windows are under-covered.
    How to read: Sort by the depth, lowest first, to find the weak windows, and check the number of targets to see whether a window is simply sparse. Look for windows that are weak in many samples. It complements the genome coverage tiles of the same module, which draw these windows along the chromosomes.

- component: figure
  title: Mean depth per contig
  description: |-
    Each bar is a contig: its mean read depth, grouped by sample and split into the whole contig (genome) and the targeted regions only (region) when mosdepth ran with a target file, with one column of panels per alignment stage (md, recal). It answers whether coverage is even between contigs.
    How to read: bars of similar height mean even coverage. A contig far below the others is under-covered, and the sex chromosomes are lower than the autosomes in a single-copy sample. Compare the region facet with the genome facet to see the enrichment of the targets.
    Lines and annotations: the last bar is the run total, a pooled row, and no line is drawn. mosdepth publishes no depth cut-off.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: chrom
    y: mean_depth
    color: sample
    barmode: group
    facet_row: scope
    facet_col: stage
    labels:
      chrom: Contig
      mean_depth: Mean depth (X)
      sample: Sample
      scope: Scope
      stage: Alignment stage

- component: card
  title: Contig mean depth
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median mean depth of a contig over the whole contig, leaving out the run total and the on-target rows, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how evenly the contigs are covered.
    How to read: a tight box means even coverage. A long lower tail holds under-covered contigs, which are usually the sex chromosomes or small contigs.
  column: mean_depth
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: (col('chrom') != 'total') & (col('scope') == 'genome')
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Coverage per contig
  description: |-
    One row is one contig of one sample, stage and scope, with its length, bases and mean, lowest and highest depth. It answers what the depth of each contig is.
    How to read: Sort by the mean depth, lowest first, to find the under- covered contigs, which are usually sex chromosomes or small contigs. Look for contigs far from the depth of the rest of the sample. It complements the per-sample depth tiles of the same output, which summarise these rows.

outputs.name: X and Y coverage sex check

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: sex_check_scatter
  title: X against Y chromosome depth
  description: |-
    Each point is a library at one alignment stage: its mean depth on chromosome X on the horizontal axis and on chromosome Y on the vertical axis, coloured by the inferred sex. It answers whether the sequenced sex agrees with the sex recorded in the sample sheet.
    How to read: libraries with two X chromosomes show strong X depth and almost no Y depth, and libraries with one X and one Y show both at a similar depth. A point that lands in the other group, or between them, can be a sample swap, a sex chromosome aneuploidy, a mixed library or a very low-depth run.
    Lines and annotations: no line is drawn. The inferred sex uses a cut-off of 10 on the X to Y depth ratio, a heuristic of this table placed between the two common karyotypes, not a published rule or a genotype call.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Mean depth on chromosome X (reads per base)
    y_title: Mean depth on chromosome Y (reads per base)
    top_n_labels: 4
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    x: x_coverage
    y: y_coverage
    label: sample
    color: inferred_sex

- component: card
  title: X to Y depth ratio
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average X to Y depth ratio over the libraries, with the lowest and highest ratio beside it. It answers how separated the libraries are into the two karyotype groups.
    How to read: a large ratio means almost no Y signal, and a ratio near 1 means one X and one Y. A wide gap between lowest and highest means the libraries belong to both groups. The ratio is read against the sample sheet, not on its own.
  column: xy_ratio
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: vertical
  caption: X to Y depth ratio, lowest and highest

- component: table
  title: Sex check
  description: |-
    One row is one library at one alignment stage, with its X and Y depth, their ratio and the inferred sex. It answers whether the sex inferred from the reads matches the sample sheet.
    How to read: Sort by the X to Y ratio to see the two groups, and compare the inferred sex with the sheet. Look for a ratio between the groups or a stage that changes the call. It complements the X against Y depth scatter of the same output, which shows these values as a plot.
